mutants.claim: maxEntryBytes is inclusive: a record of exactly the limit is written, not replaced by a notice.

expect_red.test: a record of exactly maxEntryBytes is written unchanged

mutants.claim: The same inclusive limit applies to the pipeline's own notices.

expect_red.test: a notice of exactly maxEntryBytes still fits

mutants.claim: A deletedCount arriving negative, NaN or Infinity from native is clamped to 0.

expect_red.test: a negative count is floored at zero, not passed on

mutants.claim: A fractional deletedCount is floored; rounding up invents a deleted file.

expect_red.test: a fractional count is floored, never rounded up

mutants.claim: The pending entry cap is inclusive: a buffer at the cap refuses the next record.

expect_red.test: the buffer fills to its entry cap and refuses the next record

mutants.claim: The pending byte cap is exclusive: a record filling the buffer exactly is accepted.

expect_red.test: the byte cap is exclusive, so a record filling it exactly is kept

mutants.claim: A buffer landing exactly on batchBytes pushes rather than waiting for the timer.

expect_red.test: a buffer landing exactly on batchBytes pushes without waiting

mutants.claim: hasRoom reports false at the entry cap, matching what add would do.

expect_red.test: hasRoom turns false at the entry cap, not one past it

mutants.claim: A buffer sitting on its byte cap has room for nothing: a record costs its newline.

expect_red.test: hasRoom turns false once the buffer is at the byte cap

mutants.claim: Backpressure engages when the sink queue reaches the watermark, not one byte past.

expect_red.test: the queue pauses at the watermark rather than one byte past it

mutants.claim: A record dropped by a fenced batcher is still counted, so the loss is reported.

expect_red.test: a fenced batcher counts further records as lost, never buffers them

mutants.claim: redactMetadata renders the placeholder, never the private payload, outside a dev build.

expect_red.test: the module exposes no payload-recovery export, in any position

mutants.claim: The reveal sentinel in src/ is the literal check-release-bundle.sh greps a release bundle for.

expect_red.test: the privacy reveal branch assigns the sentinel the gate greps for

mutants.claim: The sentinel is assigned only inside the __DEV__ branch, so a release bundle strips it.

expect_red.test: a release build leaves both sentinels unassigned

mutants.claim: buildCatalog is fail-closed, so catalog membership implies the key rule — which is what lets redaction skip the regex for a catalogued key.

expect_red.test: a rejected key never reaches an entry, catalog or not

mutants.claim: An unresolvable initializer falls through to the name heuristic instead of silencing every rule.

expect_red.test: the canonical name rebound through a hook no longer silences the rules

mutants.claim: A null from classifyConstruction is a decision and still ends classification, keeping loggerClassNames meaningful.

expect_red.test: narrowing loggerClassNames still silences a construction

accepted_survivors.why: The Date.now() boundary tick. Pinning it needs a clock injected into Batcher — a production change for a one-tick difference. Knowingly accepted.
